newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended with big losses on Wednesday, following Bunds down after a stream of German economic reports appeared less negative than the market had expected.

Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony later in the evening also cast a shadow over proceedings, dealers said, though some hoped for a swift reversal and the start of a cycle of advances for the Dutch market again.
"German GDP looked strongish and there is the Greenspan factor, but a lot of the weakness followed from purely technical downside testing on the (June) Bund future," one broker said.
"I think we'll soon see the start of a new period that will see us moving up again," he added.
Guilder bonds handily outperformed Bunds through the day, booking spread gains as some of yesterday's switching to Germany was reversed, dealers said.
The 10-year yield discount moved out three basis points to 0.12 percent, with the long spread out by four points to 0.22.
The rollover from the March to the June benchmark Bund future today had caused some turbulence in the market, one trader said, with the level of business otherwise "pretty normal."
However, the current rash of high-level commentary on EMU was feeding growing uncertainty over its implementation on time and would keep the market on its toes, he added.
